items.title: Telegram CEO says an extortionist planted CSAM in a chat to get it pulled from the App Store
items.raw:
Telegram CEO Pavel Durov blames an extortionist for planting child sexual abuse material (CSAM) in a public chat to get the app temporarily removed from Apple's App Store on Monday night. "Apple removed Telegram from the App Store before contacting us," Durov says in a post on X. "This creates a potential systemic risk for every mobile app that hosts user-generated content. If an app used by more than a billion people can be removed from the App Store without prior warning, any app can be."
Durov adds, "Extortionists have found a way to manipulate Apple into overreacting." Apple didn't immediately respond to The Verge's request for comment.

items.title: Skylight’s smart calendars are up to $90 off during its back-to-school sale
items.raw:
The 15-inch Skylight Calendar 2 can stand on a table or mounted to the wall. | Image: Skylight	

The start of a new school year can feel hectic, as parents juggle their kids’ classes, extracurriculars and sports on top of work, appointments, and other responsibilities. It’s easy for things to slip through the cracks, but Skylight’s shared smart calendars can help keep everyone on track, and from August 2nd through August 9th they’re up to $110 off.
The sale includes the 15-inch Skylight Calendar 2 for $279.99 ($20 off) at Best Buy and the 27-inch Skylight Calendar Max for $509.99 ($11o off) at Amazon. If you’re willing to subscribe to the $79 per year Plus plan, you can get the 10-inch Skylight Calendar for $149.99 ($20 off), which includes one month of Plus for free. The 10-inch model takes up the least amount of space, though the newer, larger 15-inch Calendar 2 features faster performance, a brighter display, and swappable magnetic frames. The 27-inch Calendar Max, meanwhile, offers the sharpest and largest screen and must be mounted to the wall (the other models can stand on a table or be mounted), making it the easiest option for large families to view from across the room. 
The Skylight Calendar

Where to Buy:

 $319.99 $299.99 at Amazon (15-inch Calendar 2)
 $299.99 $279.99 at Best Buy (15-inch Calendar 2)
 $299.99 $279.99 at Skylight (15-inch Calendar 2)

Regardless of which model you choose, every Skylight Calendar includes the same set of organizational features. Each member of your household can have their own color-coded profile, and each can sync events from Google, Outlook, Apple, Cozi, or Yahoo calendars. You can also create shared lists for groceries, chores, and other to-dos that everyone can access from the calendar or the companion mobile app, and even send your grocery list to Instacart with a couple of taps. Built-in weather forecasts also can help you plan around upcoming events, and you can also share calendar access with family members and trusted contacts. 
Skylight Calendar Max

Where to Buy:

 $619.99 $509.99 at Amazon (27-inch model)
 $629.99 $519.99 at Best Buy (27-inch model)

You get even more perks if you subscribe to the $79 per year Plus Plan (the first month of the service is free to try). Skylight uses AI to automatically turn emails, photos, flyers, and spreadsheets into calendar entries. It also adds meal planning, tools for assigning and rewarding completed chores, and a mode that displays your photos like a digital picture frame.
Read our Skylight Calendar Max review.

items.title: The Asus Chromebook Plus CX34 is at one of its lowest prices
items.raw:
The Asus Chromebook Plus CX34 is a dependable laptop that doesn’t cost a fortune, despite being nearly three years old. It’s cheaper than usual right now, and you have a few options in the sub-$400 range. The option with the most storage is currently on sale for $399.99 (about $100 off recent prices) at Amazon. It has a 12th Gen Intel Core i3 processor (1215U), 8GB of RAM, and 256GB of storage. If you don’t think you’ll need that much storage, the model with 128GB is $349.99 at Walmart, and includes a slightly faster 13th Gen Intel Core i3 processor (1315U).
Best Buy has the fastest version of the CX34 that’s discounted to $399.99. It has 8GB of RAM and 128GB of storage, but with the 13th Gen Intel Core i5 1335U. It should deliver significantly better performance compared to the i3 options above.
Asus Chromebook Plus CX34

Where to Buy:

 $499.99 $399.99 at Amazon (256GB, 12th Gen i3)
 $380 $349.99 at Walmart (128GB, 13th Gen i3)
 $729 $399.99 at Best Buy (128GB, 13th Gen i5)

The Asus Chromebook Plus CX34 is a well-built Chromebook that delivers solid performance for the price, even if its 8GB of RAM isn’t especially impressive by today’s standards. 8GB of RAM isn’t as limiting on ChromeOS as it is on Windows 11 or macOS. Its Chromebook Plus designation means it includes access to Gemini along with a free year of Google AI Pro (access to Nano Banana and Veo via Gemini, plus 5TB of storage), along with other complimentary offers. 
It’s also more powerful than many bargain bin Chromebooks; in our testing, it was snappy and responsive even with more than a dozen apps open as well as downloads and updates running in the background. We were also impressed by its sharp, 14-inch anti-glare 1080p display, along with the solid 1080p webcam. You also get a good port selection, including two USB-C ports, two USB-A ports, HDMI, and a headphone jack, so you can connect an external monitor and other devices.
Read our Asus Chromebook Plus CX34 review.
Three more ways to save
The Igloo Playmate KoolTunes 14-Quart Cooler with a built-in Bluetooth speaker is down to $69.99 ($70 off) at Walmart in a few colors, which is one of its better prices to date. It combines a classic cooler with a removable Bluetooth speaker, so you can keep drinks cold while listening to music at the beach, park, or campsite. The speaker component offers up to 10 hours of battery life and is IP56-rated for dust and water resistance, while the 14-quart cooler can hold up to 26 cans.
The Anker Charger (100W, 3 Ports, Smart Display) is on sale for $47.99 ($22 off), a new low price, with code EDF37569 at Newegg, while you can buy it for $2 more at Amazon. The small, travel-friendly charger features two USB-C ports and one USB-A port, allowing you to charge up to three devices at once with up to 100W of power. Its built-in display shows information like charging status and temperature, and Anker includes a 4.9-foot USB-C cable.
The refurbished Roborock Q7 M5 Plus is down to $192 at Roborock’s official eBay storefront when you use the code NEWFINDS20 at checkout. That’s less than half its $429.99 list price when purchased in new condition, and includes a two-year warranty. The robot vacuum and mop hybrid uses lidar navigation to map your home, allowing you to set no-go zones and clean room by room. It also comes with a self-emptying charging dock, delivers up to 10,000Pa of suction, and features an anti-tangle side brush.

items.title: Weather tracker: Austria breaks heat records as Japan braces for Typhoon Dolphin
items.raw:
Soaring temperatures continue to sweep parts of Europe, while Okinawa faces powerful winds and storm surges

Europe live – latest updates

Unbearable, record-breaking heat has dominated the summer of 2026 across much of Europe. New records were set in central Europe last week, with Wieselburg in Austria registering a new July peak of 40.3C (104.5F). This is particularly significant as it is just 0.2C behind the all-time high, set in the August of 2003.
However, not all of the northern hemisphere has experienced extreme heat and aridity. Vancouver recorded its wettest July since 2016 and the third wettest since 2008, with 33.6mm of rain. While that total may not appear exceptional, it is only a touch above the 1991-2020 climate average, highlighting how unusually dry July has been in the Canadian city over the past decade.

items.title: HIV prevention drug could reduce cases globally but USAID cuts prevent access, say experts

Injectable PrEP drug holds promise but investment in HIV prevention has declined dramatically worldwide

Sign up for the Breaking News US newsletter email 

New innovations in HIV prevention could dramatically reduce the number of new HIV cases around the globe, but US foreign aid cuts will mean that those that most need the new medication will be unable to access it, according to experts at the Aids 2026 Conference in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.
One year ago, the World Health Organization recommended that governments around the world prioritize expanded access to lenacapavir, an injectable version of the HIV prevention medication PrEP that requires only two injections annually. PrEP, which also comes in the form of daily oral medications and bimonthly injections, is 99% effective in preventing sexually transmitted HIV for people who take it consistently.
